MA.title: The job deposit
MA.brief: Dev has brought a fictional phone to the kiosk. Inspect the conversations, identify the pressure tactics, and rebuild what happened. No real money is used.
MA.closing: Case closed. You checked the evidence, named the tactics, and chose a safer response.
MA.debrief.mechanism: The sender creates a story, adds pressure, discourages outside checks, and asks for money or account access.
MA.debrief.c1: Pause before responding to a message that creates pressure.
MA.debrief.c2: Verify the claim through a contact you find independently.
MA.debrief.c3: Protect your payment details and ask a trusted person for help.
MA-E01: Earn Rs. 4,000 daily by liking three posts. No interview needed.
MA-01.explain: An easy, extraordinary earning claim is the bait.
MA-E02: I am the hiring manager. This copied company badge confirms my identity.
MA-02.explain: Copied branding is not evidence of identity.
MA-E03: Only one slot remains. Pay in the next five minutes.
MA-E04: Keep this offer secret until you have paid.
MA-04.explain: Secrecy removes opportunities to ask for help.
MA-E05: Send a joining deposit to my personal payment address.
MA-05.explain: The offer ends in a payment demand to the sender.
MA-H1: The message uses a colourful banner.
MA-H1.explain: This detail provides context but does not by itself prove a scam. Check the request and identity, not the colour or tone.
MA-H2: The message uses a smiley face.
MA-H2.explain: This detail provides context but does not by itself prove a scam. Check the request and identity, not the colour or tone.

MA.fix.q: What is the safest next step?
MA.fix.safe: Stop the conversation, verify independently, and ask a trusted person for help.
MA.fix.safe.why: This removes the pressure and gives you a reliable way to check the request.
MA.fix.pay: Send the money first and check later.
MA.fix.pay.why: Sending money first gives the sender what they want before the claim is verified.
MA.fix.share: Share the requested account details to settle the matter.
MA.fix.share.why: Account secrets and device access should stay private, regardless of the story.
MA.replay.1: The sender starts a story to attract attention.
MA.replay.2: A claimed identity or frightening statement makes the story feel important.
MA.replay.3: A deadline creates pressure to act.
MA.replay.5: The sender asks for money, secrets, or control of the device.
MA-GOLD: The sender asks for an OTP as a second way to complete the transfer.
MA-G1.explain: An OTP can expose access to an account. Keep it private and verify the request independently.
